newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. workers evacuate Zairean town after gunfire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. workers evacuate Zairean town after gunfire.

text.p: U.N. agencies started evacuating non-essential staff from the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu on Tuesday following heavy exchanges of gunfire overnight between the Rwandan army and Zairean forces.
Zaire confirmed its army traded artillery fire with Rwandan troops with material damage on both sides and one official said the situation had calmed after emergency border talks.
Brenda Barton, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) in Nairobi, told Reuters that the first plane with eight passengers left Bukavu for Nairobi at 1230 GMT.

Barton said a C-130 Hercules transport plane also left Bukavu later on Tuesday with only 24 passengers instead of 43 as planned earlier. She said some staff took flights to Goma, another eastern Zaire town, while others changed their minds and decided to stay in Bukavu.
"It is a relocation of non-essential staff because of the situation in Bukavu," Barton said.
"The idea is to minimise risk for our staff," said Fernando del Mundo, Geneva spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency which is also moving out non-essential staff.

The Rwandan army said on Tuesday it exchanged eight hours of heavy gunfire with Zairean government forces across the border town of Bukavo overnight. Emmanuel Ndahiro, Rwanda's defence ministry spokesman, said Zairean forces in Bukavu opened fire first using anti-aircraft guns and 75 mm rifles.
In Kinshasa, Zairean Foreign Minister Kititwa Tumansi accused Rwandan army units of provoking the fire-fight by pounding Bukavu with artillery on Sunday and Monday.
It was the second night of fighting between the two sides each firing from their own territory around Bukavu.
The Zairean minister said the Rwandans wanted to cut off the road linking Bukavu and Uvira, where ethnic-Rwandan Banyamulenge people accuse Zairean troops of atrocities against them.
He said Zaire had reinforced its frontier with Rwanda and intensified checks at crossing points since Monday.
The deputy governor of South Kivu Province, Lwabanji Lwasi, told Reuters by telephone from Bukavu that the city had returned to normal after emergency regional talks on Tuesday.
Lwasi said a guard was killed in Bukavu but it was not clear if he was a soldier or a civilian. There were also some wounded.
He said he met the prefect of the neighbouring Rwandan town of Cyangugu, Faustin Munyakabera, at the request of the Rwandans and "they have undertaken to stop the firing".

Zaire's relations with Rwanda have been poor since 1994 but have worsened recently. More than one million Rwandan Hutu refugees live in camps in eastern Zaire from where Rwanda says they mount guerrilla incursions.
The Hutus fled their homeland fearing reprisals for the genocide in 1994 of up to one million minority Tutsis and pro-opposition Hutus in Rwanda.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said it would continue to operate there despite the fighting.
The International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) pulled out three of its seven foreign staff in Bukavu on Monday.

The firing followed the Zairean government stepping up its campaign against neighbours Rwanda and Burundi and aid agencies by accusing them of promoting or aiding armed Tutsi infiltrators on missions to destabilise its volatile eastern refugee zone.
The government warned aid agencies caring for the estimated 1.1 million Rwandan Hutu refugees in camps in eastern Zaire that they would be banned unless they limited themselves to aid work.
Human rights watchdog Amnesty International on Friday accused Zairean troops and officials of atrocities against Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Zaire over the past month.
There are some 400,000 Banyamulenge, all of whom claim to be Zairean.
